title: Student visa (subclass 500): With this visa you can
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), With this visa you can: participate in an eligible course of study in Australia. travel in and out of Australia. work up to 48 hours a fortnight when your course of study or training is in session.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): How long you can stay
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), How long you can stay: Up to 6 years and in line with your enrolment.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Cost
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Cost: Cost concession. A lower visa cost applies to eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste citizens, eligible ASEAN citizens and applicants in the ELICOS and Non-Award sector who lodge a valid Student visa application. See About this visa. To work out what your visa will cost, use the Visa Pricing Estimator. The estimator does not take into account the other costs.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): You must
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), You must: apply online. apply from outside Australia unless you hold an eligible visa and meet an exemption allowing you to apply in Australia. be enrolled in a course of study in Australia and hold a valid Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) when we decide your visa. hold Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC), or fall in one of the exemption categories. be 6 years or older. prove you have a welfare arrangement, if you are under 18. not bring family members (partners and children) to Australia, unless exempt. Note: A CoE is no longer valid if it is cancelled or the course is complete.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): You must
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), You must: A substantive visa ceases to be in effect if another substantive visa is granted. Applications are received Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST) (or Australian Eastern daylight standard time (AEDST) when applicable). Help with your visa. If you are getting help with your visa, before you pay someone, read information on Who can help with your visa application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Be a certain age (school student)
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Be a certain age (school student): If you are a school student (but not participating in a secondary school student exchange program), you must be aged 6 or older to apply for this visa. You must also be: less than 17 years old when you begin Year 9. less than 18 years old when you begin Year 10. less than 19 years old when you begin Year 11. less than 20 years old when you begin Year 12.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence: You must include the right evidence of enrolment in study with your Student visa application, or your application will not be valid and can't be processed. Providing a Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE). You must be enrolled in a full time course registered on the Commonwealth Register of Institutions and courses for Overseas Students (CRICOS). You must provide a Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) for all intended courses when you apply. If you do not provide a CoE at time of lodgement, the student visa application will be invalid. Your CoE must be valid when we decide your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence: A CoE is no longer valid if it is cancelled or the course is complete. If you finish your course, but still require a student visa, you will need to attach a new CoE to your ImmiAccount. You must maintain enrolment in a course of study to be eligible for a student visa. Packaged courses and CoEs. If you are applying for more than one (1) course in your Student visa application, you must include all CoE codes in the application form, as your visa period may only consider the duration of the course according to the CoE provided.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence: You can apply to include two (2) or more courses on your Student visa where one course clearly leads to the next. Course gaps must be less than two calendar months, unless the first course finishes at the end of the standard academic year and the next course commences at the beginning of the standard academic year. If you want your Student visa to cover more than one (1) course you must include all CoE codes in your visa application form, or your visa may only cover the CoE provided.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence: If you are a student visa holder and you meet an exemption to lodge a further Student visa in Australia, you cannot package courses together unless you are applying for: primary or secondary school studies, or. a further visa because your education provider defaulted. In all other scenarios, you can only apply in Australia for one further course. Other evidence of enrolment.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Be enrolled in a course of study and provide evidence: You do not need to provide a Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) if you are: enrolled in a full-time course of study or training under a scholarship scheme approved by the Australian Minister for Foreign Affairs and Trade: provide a letter of support. sponsored by the Australian Department of Defence: provide a letter of support. a secondary exchange student: provide an Acceptance Advice of Secondary Exchange Student (AASES) form. a postgraduate research student who needs to stay in Australia while your thesis is marked: provide a letter from your education provider.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Make Welfare arrangements if you are under 18 years
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Make Welfare arrangements if you are under 18 years: If you are applying for a Student visa and you are under 18 years of age, you must have adequate welfare arrangements in place while you are in Australia. If you will be 18 years of age when you arrive in Australia, you must tell us as you might not need to provide some of this information. To learn more, see Welfare arrangements for students under 18.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Meet English language requirements
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Meet English language requirements: You might need to provide evidence of your English language skills when you submit your visa application. If you need to provide evidence of your English language skills, you must prove that you: have obtained a certain test score in an English language test that the Department has approved, or. fall into an exemption category listed below. For more information on the minimum overall band scores you must achieve to meet the Student visa English language requirements, go to Gather Documents in the 'Step by Step' tab.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Meet English language requirements
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Meet English language requirements: To find out if you need to provide evidence of your English language skills when you apply, use the Document Checklist tool.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): English language tests
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), English language tests: You must have completed the English language test: within the 2 years before you lodged your visa application, if you are Regular Evidence level; or. within the 2 years before a decision is made on your visa application, if you are Streamlined Evidence level and the Department has requested evidence. At-home or online English language tests. The Department of Home Affairs does not accept evidence from English language tests where an entire test is delivered online (also known as “remote-proctored” or “at-home”).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): English language tests
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), English language tests: Examples of online tests that are not approved for Australian visa purposes, include: IELTS Online. LANGUAGECERT Academic Online. OET@Home. CELPIP Online. MET Digital (taken at-home). TOEFL iBT – Home Edition. TOEFL iBT. From 21 January 2026, applicants must select 'Taking TOEFL for Australia ’ during registration to ensure the test is valid for Australian visa purposes. We will not accept TOEFL iBT tests completed between 26 July 2023, and 4 May 2024 for Australian visa and migration purposes. During this period, the TOEFL iBT test being offered was not an approved test.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): English language tests
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), English language tests: Cambridge C1 Advanced test (previously known as Cambridge English: Advanced CAE). From 12 February 2024 to 6 August 2025, the department will only accept results from the Cambridge C1 Advanced paper-based test. The department will still accept tests taken before 12 February 2024 and within specified validity periods, for C1 Advanced paper-based and computer-based tests. LANGUAGECERT Academic. If you sit a LANGUAGECERT test, you will receive a ‘certificate’ and a ‘report’.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): English language tests
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), English language tests: If you use your LANGUAGECERT Academic results to show you meet the English language requirement, you must include both documents with your visa application. If you do not provide the certificate and the report, visa processing may be delayed.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): English language evidence exemptions
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), English language evidence exemptions: You do not need to give us evidence of an English test score with your visa application if one of the following applies: you are a citizen and hold a passport from UK, USA, Canada, NZ or Republic of Ireland. you are an applicant who is a Foreign Affairs or Defence sponsored student, or a Secondary Exchange student (AASES). you are enrolled in a principal course of study that is a registered school course. you are enrolled in a principal course of study that is a standalone English Language Intensive Course for Overseas Students (ELICOS). you are enrolled in a principal course of study registered and delivered in a language other than English. you are enrolled in a registered post-graduate research course. you have completed at least 5 years’ study in English in Australia, UK, USA, Canada, New Zealand, South Africa, or the Republic of Ireland. in the 2 years before applying for the Student visa you completed the Senior Secondary Certificate of Education in Australia in English while you held a Student visa. in the 2 years before applying for the Student visa you completed a substantial component of a course that would qualify you under the Australian Qualifications Framework at the Certificate IV or higher level, while you held a Student visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): English language evidence exemptions
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), English language evidence exemptions: Note: We may need you to give us evidence of an English test score with your visa application if you hold a British National Overseas (BNO) passport. If you are required to provide evidence of English language proficiency but you fall into an exemption category, make sure you provide the appropriate evidence that demonstrates that you satisfy one of the exemptions. For more information on English Language Tests and Evidence Exemptions refer to the Migration (English Language Tests and Evidence Exemptions for Subclass 500 (Student) Visas) Instrument 2025 - Federal Register of Legislation.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Have adequate health insurance
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Have adequate health insurance: You and your family members must have and maintain adequate health insurance for the whole of your stay in Australia. To find out the length of coverage you will require, see Student visa grant periods. You and your family members must be covered by Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) from an approved Australian health insurance provider, unless an 'Exception' applies. Applicants outside Australia. Your cover must start from the day you and your family arrive in Australia, not the day your course starts.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Have adequate health insurance
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Have adequate health insurance: If you have been granted a visa and want to travel to Australia before your course begins, the OSHC start date must be the same as the date you arrive, not the date your course starts. Generally this is a minimum of 1 week to 1 month before your course starts. You must: ensure you don't enter Australia before your OSHC begins, and. maintain your OSHC until you leave Australia. You may be refused entry to Australia if you cannot prove you have health insurance in place when you arrive. Applicants in Australia. Applicants must have OSHC.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Have adequate health insurance
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Have adequate health insurance: If your previous visa required you to have health insurance, cover must be continuous with no gap between your previous health cover and your OSHC. Exceptions. You do not need to have OSHC if you are: a Norwegian student covered by the Norwegian National Insurance Scheme. a Swedish student covered by Kammarkollegiet. a Belgian student covered under the Reciprocal Health Care Agreement with Australia. How to get Overseas Student Health Cover. To get OSHC: find an approved provider. pay for your policy. Your education provider or agent might arrange OSHC for you.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Have adequate health insurance
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Have adequate health insurance: If your education provider arranges your OSHC coverage, you will need to know the name of your health insurance provider, the date that your policy starts and finishes and should be aware of the terms and conditions of your policy. Your education provider will also need to include your health insurance information on your Certificate of Enrolment (CoE). If you arrange OSHC coverage yourself, you will need to know the policy number to include in the visa application. We will refuse your visa application if you don't give us this information when you apply for your Student visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Have adequate health insurance
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Have adequate health insurance: Insurance for family members. If you have a single OSHC policy and you have family members, including children born in Australia after your arrival, consider getting a family policy. Every member of your family must have health insurance. Any family member who joins you after you arrive in Australia must show us they have OSHC for the duration of their stay in Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Apply from the right location
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Apply from the right location: From 2 October 2026, new rules mean that most Student visa applications must be lodged outside Australia. You can only apply in Australia if you hold an eligible visa and meet an exemption category. Eligible visas. If you hold a visa as a primary or secondary holder on the list below you cannot apply for a student visa in Australia. There are no exemptions to this rule. Subclass 400 – Temporary Work (all streams). Subclass 403 – (Domestic Worker – Diplomatic/Consular stream). Subclass 407 – Training (all streams). Subclass 408 – Temporary Activity (all streams).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Apply from the right location
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Apply from the right location: Subclass 417 – Working Holiday (all streams). Subclass 457 – Temporary Work (all streams). Subclass 462 – Work and Holiday (all streams). Subclass 482 – Skills in Demand / Temporary Skill Shortage (all streams). Subclass 485 – Temporary Graduate. Subclass 600 – Visitor. Subclass 601 – ETA. Subclass 602 – Medical Treatment. Subclass 651 – eVisitor. Subclass 771 – Transit. Subclass 988 – Maritime Crew. Subclass 995 – Diplomatic (Temporary) (primary only. A family member of a Diplomatic (Temporary) visa (subclass 995) can apply for a Student visa in Australia).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Meet an exemption to apply for a further student visa in Australia
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Meet an exemption to apply for a further student visa in Australia: If you are student visa holder you may be able to apply for another Student visa while in Australia. Dependent or secondary student visa holders cannot apply for a student visa as the primary applicant while in Australia. If you hold a student visa as the primary applicant, you may be able to apply in Australia if you meet one of the six exemptions below. If you do not meet an exemption, you should not apply in Australia. We will not accept your application if you are not eligible and this may have consequences if you are in Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Meet an exemption to apply for a further student visa in Australia
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Meet an exemption to apply for a further student visa in Australia: An invalid application outcome could affect your visa status and you may not be eligible to apply for a further visa if your visa has already expired. Invalid decisions cannot be merits reviewed at the ART.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 1 – you need up to 12 additional months to complete your studies.
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 1 – you need up to 12 additional months to complete your studies.: To apply under this exemption: you need up to 12 additional months from the original end date of your main course to finish your course, and. the course you are completing must be the main course in your package of courses (if you are studying packaged courses), and. the course must be with the same education provider that your current Student visa was granted for (you can have changed courses but the course you changed to must be at the same AQF level or higher).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 1 – you need up to 12 additional months to complete your studies.
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 1 – you need up to 12 additional months to complete your studies.: For example, students who have started a Bachelor’s Degree can apply for a student visa in Australia if they need up to 12 extra months to finish the same degree or a different Bachelor agree at the same education provider. Understanding AQF levels and VET courses. The Australian qualifications are ranked from level 1 to level 10 by the Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF). Check the AQF level of your current and proposed course to see whether you meet the course completion exemption.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 2 – you are sponsored by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) or Defence
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 2 – you are sponsored by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) or Defence: To apply under this exemption, you must be sponsored by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade or the Department of Defence.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 3 – you are applying to undertake a PhD
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 3 – you are applying to undertake a PhD: To apply under this exemption, you must be applying to study a Doctoral Degree (PhD). You cannot apply under this exemption if you are applying to study a Master’s by Research course.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 4 – you are applying to undertake primary or secondary school studies
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 4 – you are applying to undertake primary or secondary school studies: To apply under this exemption, you must be applying to study primary or secondary school studies.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course: To apply under this exemption: you must have completed your main course for which your visa was granted for or you have completed a course which was the same or higher AQF level as the original course your student visa was granted for, and. you are progressing to a course at a higher AQF level, and. if your completed course was a higher education course, the course you are progressing to must also be a higher education course delivered by a higher education provider.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course: You can also apply for this exemption: if the main course you completed did not have an AQF level, and you are progressing to a course with an AQF level or. you have completed your school studies and are progressing to a course that does not have an AQF level. For example: Students who have completed an English Language Intensive Courses for Overseas Students (ELICOS) course can apply for a student visa in Australia if they are progressing to a Bachelor’s Degree.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course: Students who have completed an ELICOS course cannot apply for a student visa in Australia if they want to study another ELICOS course. Students who have completed their secondary school studies can apply for a student visa in Australia if they want to study a foundational course after they finish school. Students who have completed a Bachelor’s Degree at a higher education provider cannot apply for a student visa in Australia if they want to study a Graduate Diploma course at a VET provider. Understanding AQF levels and VET courses.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 5 – you have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course: The Australian qualifications are ranked from level 1 to level 10 by the Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF). Check the AQF level of your current and proposed course to see whether you meet the course progression exemption.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 6 – you cannot continue your course because your education provider has defaulted
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 6 – you cannot continue your course because your education provider has defaulted: To apply under this exemption, you must be unable to continue your course because your education provider has defaulted. For more information, see Education provider default.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Meet an exemption if you want to include family members
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Meet an exemption if you want to include family members: If you meet one of the exemptions below, your family members must apply at the same time and from the same location as you. If your family members are applying with you in Australia, they must hold an eligible visa to apply. If you do not meet an exemption to include family, you should not lodge an application for your family members. We will not accept your family member’s application if they are not eligible and this may have consequences if they are in Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Meet an exemption if you want to include family members
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Meet an exemption if you want to include family members: An invalid application outcome could affect their visa status and they may not be eligible to apply for a further visa if their visa has already expired. Invalid decisions cannot be merits reviewed at the ART.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 1 – you are a Doctoral (PhD) student
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 1 – you are a Doctoral (PhD) student: To include family under this exemption, you must be applying to study a Doctoral Degree (PhD). You cannot apply under this exemption if you are applying to study a Master’s by Research course. You can include family members when you lodge your visa application inside or outside Australia. If your family members are applying in Australia, they must hold an eligible visa or a student visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 2 – you are a Department of Defence or Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade sponsored student
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 2 – you are a Department of Defence or Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade sponsored student: To include family under this exemption, you must be sponsored by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade or the Department of Defence. You can include family members when you lodge your visa application inside or outside Australia. If your family members are applying in Australia, they must hold an eligible visa or a student visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 3 – you are a foreign government scholarship recipient
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 3 – you are a foreign government scholarship recipient: To include family under this exemption, you must be receiving a foreign government scholarship that fully funds your studies in Australia. If you are outside Australia, you can include family members when you lodge your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 3 – you are a foreign government scholarship recipient
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 3 – you are a foreign government scholarship recipient: If you are inside Australia, you can only include family members when you lodge your application if you: need up to 12 additional months to complete the main course covered by your current Student visa, or. have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course at a higher Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) level. if your completed course was a higher education course, the course you are progressing to must also be a higher education course delivered by a higher education provider, or. need to lodge a further Student visa application because your education provider defaulted.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 4 – Eligible national from Pacific Island or ASEAN countries
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 4 – Eligible national from Pacific Island or ASEAN countries: To include family under this exemption, you must be a national from a Pacific Island: Federated States of Micronesia. Kiribati. Papua New Guinea. Republic of the Marshall Islands. Solomon Islands. Vanuatu. Or an ASEAN country: Brunei Darussalam. Cambodia. Indonesia. Lao Peoples Dem Republic. Malaysia. Myanmar. Philippines. Singapore. Thailand. Timor-Leste. Vietnam. If you are outside Australia, you can include family members when you lodge your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 4 – Eligible national from Pacific Island or ASEAN countries
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 4 – Eligible national from Pacific Island or ASEAN countries: If you are inside Australia, you can only include family members when you lodge your application if you: need up to 12 additional months to complete the main course covered by your current Student visa, or. have completed your main course and are applying in Australia to undertake another course at a higher Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) level.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 4 – Eligible national from Pacific Island or ASEAN countries
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 4 – Eligible national from Pacific Island or ASEAN countries: If your completed course was a higher education course, the course you are progressing to must also be a higher education course delivered by a higher education provider, or. need to lodge a further Student visa application because your education provider defaulted.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 5 – Other exemptions
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 5 – Other exemptions: Current Student visa holders applying inside or outside Australia. If you currently hold a Student visa and you are inside or outside Australia, you can include family members who are currently on your Student visa when you lodge your application, if: you need up to 12 additional months to complete your main course covered by your current Student visa, or. you need to lodge a further Student visa application because your education provider defaulted. Current student visa holders applying inside Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 5 – Other exemptions
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 5 – Other exemptions: If you currently hold a student visa and you are inside Australia, you can include family members who are currently on your student visa when you lodge your application, if: you have completed your main course for which your student visa was granted for or you have completed a course which was the same or higher AQF level as the original course your student visa was granted for, and. you are progressing to a course at a higher AQF level, and. if your completed course was a higher education course, the course you are progressing to must also be a higher education course delivered by a higher education provider.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Exemption 5 – Other exemptions
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Exemption 5 – Other exemptions: You can also apply for this exemption: if the main course you completed did not have an AQF level, and you are progressing to a course with an AQF level or. you have completed your school studies and are progressing to a course that does not have an AQF level. You must have held or applied for a Student visa before 2 October 2026.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Have enough money for your stay
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Have enough money for your stay: You must have enough money to pay for your stay in Australia. To see the minimum amount of money you need for your visa application go to 'Gather Documents' under Step by Step. The living costs we ask you to declare and provide with your visa application is the minimum amount of money you need for the visa. Actual living costs vary throughout Australia. They may be much higher than what you need for the visa. We recommend you research the area you intend to live including the cost of living in that area. You should not rely on work to support yourself or your family while in Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Have enough money for your stay
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Have enough money for your stay: The Australian Government Study Australia website provides useful information on accommodation options. It features a cost of living calculator to help you consider other possible costs in addition to the amount required for your visa application. For more information visit Study Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Be a genuine student
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Be a genuine student: You must: be a genuine student for entry. be able to show an understanding that studying in Australia is the primary reason of your Student visa. For more information, see Genuine Student requirement.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Meet our character requirement
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Meet our character requirement: You and family members aged 16 years and over who apply for the visa must meet our character requirement.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Meet our health requirement
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Meet our health requirement: You and any family members who apply for the visa must meet our health requirement.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Sign the Australian values statement

title: Student visa (subclass 500): Evidence you have enough money for your stay
abstract: Student visa (subclass 500), Evidence you have enough money for your stay: If you are in Australia and your course has already started, calculate the course fee for 12 months starting on the date you lodge your application. Example 1: your course fee is AUD50,000 for 3 years. The fee for 12 months is the total course cost divided by the number of years you will be studying. AUD50,000 divided by 3 years = AUD16,666, less any amount you have already paid if relevant. Example 2: your course fee is AUD15,000 for 10 months and you have already paid AUD5,000. Deduct the amount you have already paid from the total amount. AUD15,000 - AUD5,000 = AUD10,000.

Anyone with a legal right to decide where you live, and who is not travelling in Australia with you, must complete either: Form 1229 - Consent form to grant an Australian visa to a child under the age of 18 years. a statutory declaration giving their consent for you to visit Australia on this visa.

Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited. Note: You do not need to have any documents certified unless we ask you to.

abstract: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601), Have an eligible passport: You must hold a valid passport from one of these countries or jurisdictions to be eligible for an ETA. Hong Kong (SAR of China). Iceland. Ireland. Liechtenstein. Luxembourg. Malaysia. Portugal. Republic of San Marino. Singapore. South Korea. Switzerland. Near-field communication (NFC) enabled on your mobile device. Location services enabled on your mobile device. A valid email address. A valid payment method ready to pay the service fee. abstract: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601), Other ways to apply: If you are ineligible or unable to apply for an ETA using the Australian ETA app, you can apply online for another visa that suits your needs through ImmiAccount. European passport holders may be eligible for an eVisitor (subclass 651) visa. There is no charge to make an eVisitor visa application. attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601): Provide accurate information
abstract: Electronic Travel Authority (subclass 601), Provide accurate information: When applying, you must truthfully answer all questions. This includes declaring: if you hold any other passports. if you have been known by any other name. any criminal conviction or domestic violence history. If you do not provide accurate information, we may cancel your ETA. If your ETA details do not exactly match your passport details, you might experience delays when boarding your aircraft or be refused entry in Australia. We cannot change the details on an ETA once it has been issued. We suggest you do not make travel arrangements until we grant your ETA.

Your application might take longer to process if: you don't fill it in correctly. we need more information from you. your information is hard to verify. If you have a criminal conviction in any country, we will need more information from you. You should apply for a Visitor (subclass 600) visa and provide evidence about your criminal convictions.

abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Enough money for your stay and to leave: Provide evidence you have enough money for your stay in Australia. This is usually AUD5,000. You must also show us you have enough money to buy a ticket to leave Australia at the end of your stay, or that you already have the ticket. If you are applying in Australia, you don’t need to provide evidence. If you are applying outside Australia and don’t attach evidence to your application, processing may be delayed if we need to contact you to request further information.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa: Proof of specified subclass 417 work
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), second Working Holiday visa, Proof of specified subclass 417 work: Provide proof that you have completed 3 months of specified subclass 417 work on your previous WHM visa (or in other eligible circumstances). The proof must cover all periods you worked. You can include any of the following: pay slips. Australian bank statements covering the period of declared specified work. piece rate agreement with your employer, if you were paid piece rates. The agreement must show the pay rate per piece and how it is measured. group certificates. payment summaries. tax returns. employer references. a written and signed agreement setting out any lawful deductions in pay.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

We will not process your application until you pay the fee. Note the Transaction reference number. Applicants with dependent children. You can’t apply online if you are the parent of a child under the age of 18. Working Holiday visa holders cannot be accompanied by dependent children at any time during their stay in Australia. While it is possible to obtain a Working Holiday visa if you have a child, your child cannot join you in Australia at any time while you are on your Working Holiday visa – not even for one day.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), third Working Holiday visa: You applied in Australia
abstract: Working Holiday visa (subclass 417), third Working Holiday visa, You applied in Australia: Tell us if you want to travel outside Australia while we process your application. We need to know because you must be in Australia when we decide your application. If you leave Australia, make sure you have a valid visa to return. You can travel outside Australia and return as many times as you want while the visa is in effect. Time spent outside Australia after your visa commences does not extend the visa period of stay in Australia.

abstract: Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), Post-Higher Education Work stream, Have this visa: You must be in Australia (but not in immigration clearance) when you apply for this visa. Subsequent entrants can be in or outside Australia when they apply. We will process your visa application if: you are in Australia and hold an eligible Student visa (not one supported by the Minister for Defence or the Minister for Foreign Affairs and Trade). you held a Student visa within the past 6 months and now hold a Bridging Visa A or Bridging Visa B granted based on a valid visa application. you held a Student visa within the past 6 months and now hold a substantive visa.

title: Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), Post-Higher Education Work stream: Have this visa
abstract: Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), Post-Higher Education Work stream, Have this visa: To be eligible for this visa you must have completed your course within 6 months of applying. If you previously held a subclass 485 or 476 visa as a primary applicant, you cannot be granted this visa as a primary applicant again. If you held one of these visas as a secondary applicant, you may be eligible to apply as a primary applicant.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), Post-Higher Education Work stream: Hold an eligible qualification at degree-level or above
abstract: Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), Post-Higher Education Work stream, Hold an eligible qualification at degree-level or above: You must have been awarded an eligible degree, regardless of your field of study, in the 6 months immediately before the day you apply for your visa. attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), Post-Higher Education Work stream: Qualifications
abstract: Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), Post-Higher Education Work stream, Qualifications: The qualification that you have completed must be an eligible degree. This means a: Bachelor degree. Bachelor honours degree. Masters (coursework) degree. Masters (extended) degree. Masters (research) degree. Doctoral degree (research). Doctoral degree (professional). Higher doctoral degree. A graduate diploma is considered an eligible degree if: you completed it in the same or next academic year as your successfully completed qualification (listed above) and. the study is related to that qualification.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), Post-Higher Education Work stream: Meet the Temporary Graduate visa study requirement
abstract: Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), Post-Higher Education Work stream, Meet the Temporary Graduate visa study requirement: You must have been awarded an eligible degree, regardless of your field of study, in the 6 months immediately before the day you apply for your visa and meet the Temporary Graduate visa study requirement. On 25 November 2023, online study requirements returned to their pre-COVID state. Online study undertaken during the COVID concession period (1 February 2020 to 25 November 2023) will continue to count towards the Temporary Graduate visa study requirement. For more information about eligible study see the Temporary Graduate visa study requirement.

title: Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), Post-Higher Education Work stream: Character documents
abstract: Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), Post-Higher Education Work stream, Character documents: You and any other applicants aged 16 years or over must provide evidence that you applied for an Australian Federal Police (AFP) check within the 12 month period ending the day before you submit your visa application. This means: you must not apply for the AFP check on the same day as your visa application. you must apply for the AFP check no earlier than 12 months before and no later than the day before your visa application date. We only accept complete disclosure National Police Certificates (Immigration/Citizenship – Australia Name Check Only) issued by the Australian Federal Police.

The AFP application submission confirmation page can be saved and used as evidence of the date you applied for the AFP check. title: Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), Post-Higher Education Work stream: Dependants under 18 documents
abstract: Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), Post-Higher Education Work stream, Dependants under 18 documents: They must complete either: Form 1229 Consent form to grant an Australian visa to a child under the age of 18 years. a statutory declaration giving their consent for the child to visit Australia on this visa. abstract: Skilled Independent visa (subclass 189), Points-tested stream, Get your skills assessed: You must have a suitable skills assessment at the time we invite you to apply. title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Stay lawful
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Stay lawful: An EOI is not a visa application. Submitting an EOI does not mean you will get a bridging visa. If your current visa is about to expire, you must apply for another visa to remain in Australia lawfully. You are not eligible for a bridging visa because the EOI is not a visa application. You are only eligible for a bridging visa after you are invited and apply for this visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Make changes to your EOI
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Make changes to your EOI: Let us know through SkillSelect if: you want to apply for a different skilled visa. your circumstances change - for example, if you change your occupation or your family structure changes. you could score more points - for example, you have completed a higher qualification or gained new work experience. your employment circumstances change and you are no longer working at least 20 hours per week in your nominated occupation. You must be able to meet the points score on your invitation letter if we invite you to apply.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Make changes to your EOI
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Make changes to your EOI: SkillSelect will update your indicative points score when you make changes to your EOI. You can change your EOI at any time before we invite you to apply for a visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Step 1.4 – Receive an invitation to apply for visa
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Step 1.4 – Receive an invitation to apply for visa: We allocate places for the skilled migration program to meet the Australian Government’s migration planning levels. Once invited, you have 60 calendar days to apply for the visa. We cannot extend this time. You could receive an invitation up to 2 years after submitting an EOI. If we invite you to apply you will receive an email from SkillSelect. Getting an invitation does not mean you will be granted the visa. The invitation will include an indicative points score based on your EOI claims.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Step 1.4 – Receive an invitation to apply for visa
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Step 1.4 – Receive an invitation to apply for visa: When you apply for the visa, you must show that you: can meet the points score on your invitation (which will include proving any claims you made in your EOI) and. can meet all other eligibility criteria. If you do not apply for the visa after two invitations, your EOI will be removed from SkillSelect. We will not process your visa application if you are 45 or over at the time of your invitation.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): If you can't show you meet the invited points score or other eligibility criteria
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), If you can't show you meet the invited points score or other eligibility criteria: If you can't show you meet the points score on your invitation or the other visa criteria, then do not apply for the visa. Your EOI will be suspended if an invitation is issued, but you can update information once the 60-day invitation period has passed. If this is your second invitation, you will have to submit another EOI if you still want the visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Get help with your application
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Get help with your application: Only some people can help you with your application. If you appoint someone to give you immigration assistance they must be: a registered migration agent. a legal practitioner, or. an exempt person. You can appoint anyone to receive documents on your behalf relating to your visa matter.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Gather your documents: You will need to provide documents to support the claims you make in your EOI and show you meet the other visa criteria.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Provide accurate information
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Provide accurate information: Provide accurate information. See what happens if you can't prove your identity or do not provide true information.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Identity documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Identity documents: Provide the pages of your current passport showing your photo, personal details, and passport issue and expiry dates. Also provide: a national identity card, if you have one. proof of change of name. Documents that prove a change of name include: a marriage or divorce certificate. change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority. documents that show other names you have been known by.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Relationship documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Relationship documents: If you are or have been married, widowed, divorced or permanently separated, provide proof such as divorce documents, death certificates, separation documents or statutory declarations. If your partner or dependent children are not included in this application, tell us the reason why (for example, they already hold Australian citizenship or are a permanent resident).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Character documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Character documents: Provide an Australian police certificate if you have spent a total of 12 months or more in Australia in the last 10 years since you turned 16. We only accept complete disclosure National Police Certificates issued by the Australian Federal Police. We do not accept standard disclosure certificates or national police certificates issued by Australian state or territory police. For immigration purposes, Australian police certificates are valid for 12 months from the date of issue.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Character documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Character documents: Also provide: an overseas police certificate from every country, including your home country, where you spent a total of 12 months or more in the last 10 years since you turned 16. military service records or discharge papers if you served in the armed forces of any country. Complete and provide the following forms: Form 80 – Personal particulars for character assessment. Form 1221 Additional personal particulars information.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Competent English documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Competent English documents: Provide proof you have at least competent English at time of invitation for this.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Partner documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Partner documents: We need to see evidence of your partner's identity and relationship with you. Provide: identity documents and photos. character documents. marriage certificate, if applicable. documents about other relationships, if applicable. For de facto relationship provide either: evidence that your relationship is registered by an Australian State or Territory. enough documents to prove you have been in a de facto relationship with your partner for at least 12 months before you apply. For both married and de facto applicants you must provide evidence that you are in a genuine and continuing relationship.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Partner documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Partner documents: Evidence can include but is not limited to: joint bank account statements. billing accounts in joint names. joint leases or mortgages. documents that show your partner has lived at the same address as you.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Proof your partner has functional English
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Proof your partner has functional English: Provide proof that your partner has at least functional English.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): If you can't provide functional English documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), If you can't provide functional English documents: If any of the dependent applicants, who did not pay the second instalment cannot show evidence of functional English, you will need to pay the second instalment of the visa application charge for each of those dependent applicants, when we ask you to.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Dependants under 18 documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Dependants under 18 documents: For every dependant 18 years old or younger who is applying with you, provide: copies of birth certificates or the family book showing the names of both parents of all your dependent children. copies of the adoption paper, if applicable.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Parental responsibility documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Parental responsibility documents: You must get consent for a dependent child to migrate to Australia from anyone who: You must get consent for any applicant under 18 years of age to migrate to Australia from anyone who: has a legal right to decide where the child lives and. is not coming to Australia with the child. They must complete either: Form 1229 Consent form to grant an Australian visa to a child under the age of 18 years. statutory declaration giving their consent for the child to migrate to Australia on this visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Parental responsibility documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Parental responsibility documents: Alternatively, you can show us: an Australian court order that allows your child to migrate to Australia, or. that the laws of your home country allow them to migrate. Include: an identity document that shows the signature and photo of the person who completed the form or declaration, such as a passport or driver’s licence. adoption papers or other court documents if applicable. You don't have to prove that your dependant under 18 years of age has functional English.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Parental responsibility documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Parental responsibility documents: Note: If your child is likely to turn 18 while your application is being processed, you will need to provide evidence they are dependent on you. See the section 'Dependants over 18 documents' below for further information. A child who turns 18 while your application is being processed and who is not dependent on you cannot satisfy the criteria for this visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Dependants over 18 documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Dependants over 18 documents: To include your child who is over 18 in your visa application, they must be: over 18 years of age but not yet turned 23, and dependent on you or your partner, or. over 23 years of age and unable to earn a living to support themselves due to physical or cognitive limitations and dependent on you or your partner. If your child is likely to turn 23 while your application is being processed, you will need to provide evidence they are dependent on you due to disability. Provide: identity documents. documents about their other relationships, if applicable.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Dependants over 18 documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Dependants over 18 documents: You must also provide proof the child is dependent on you. proof of your relationship with the dependant such as a birth certificate or adoption papers. a completed Form 47a Details of a child or other dependent family member aged 18 years or over. proof of financial dependency such as bank statements, money transfers and rent receipts. if the child is aged 23 or is likely to turn 23 while your application is being processed, you must also provide a report from a qualified medical practitioner that states they are dependent on you or your partner due to the total or partial loss of their bodily or mental functions.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Dependants over 18 documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Dependants over 18 documents: Note: A child who turns 23 while your application is being processed and who does not meet these requirements cannot satisfy the criteria for this visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Proof your dependant has functional English
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Proof your dependant has functional English: Provide proof that all dependent applicants aged 18 years and older, have at least functional English.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Skills assessment documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Skills assessment documents: You must provide documents that support the claims you made in your EOI. To check the documents you need use the points table. Depending on your claims this could include evidence of your: skills assessment. English language skills. Australian and/or overseas skilled employment. educational qualifications. Satisfying the Australian study requirement. specialist education. accredited community language. study in regional Australia. partner skills. Professional Year in Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Skills assessment documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Skills assessment documents: Delegates of the Minister will now accept a suitable skills assessment for an applicant’s nominated skilled occupation which has been obtained within the 60 day invitation period. This change of approach is made as a result of the decision of Thapa v Minister for Immigration, Citizenship, Migrant Services and Multicultural Affairs [2021] FCCA 686 ( Thapa ). The Minister will administer the Migration Regulations 1994 in accordance with the decision in Thapa, but the Minister reserves the right to make submissions in a Court that Thapa was wrongly decided.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Medical practitioners
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Medical practitioners: One of these certificates issued by the Australian Health Practitioner Regulation Agency: unconditional or general medical registration. conditional specialist registration – which allows you to practice only in your speciality with no further training or supervision requirements. You must be registered at the time we invite you to apply.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Barristers and Solicitors
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Barristers and Solicitors: Proof of admission to practice as a lawyer in the relevant state or territory. This could be your Australian legal Admission Certificate or Practising Certificate from the relevant legal admission authority for your State/Territory. You must be admitted to practice at the time we invite you to apply.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Expression of interest (EOI) documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Expression of interest (EOI) documents: You must provide documents to prove all of the claims you made in your EOI. Use the points table to check the documents you need.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Employment Documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Employment Documents: To claim points for skilled employment experience, you must provide evidence of the employment period you are claiming. The evidence must relate to employment before the date of invitation. Evidence can include: employment references. employment contracts. payslips. tax statements. group certificates or payment summaries. superannuation information.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Employment Documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Employment Documents: Employment references must: be issued on the organisation’s official letterhead. include the organisation’s full street address, not a PO Box. include the organisation’s phone number, email address and website, where available. show the exact period of employment. state each position held. state whether the employment was permanent or temporary, and full time or part time. describe main duties. state the salary earned. include the typed or stamped name and position of the person authorised to sign the reference below their signature. include the direct contact number of the person writing the reference.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Employment Documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Employment Documents: We will not accept a reference that only includes an illegible signature.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Sponsor documents: If you are being sponsored, provide: Skilled Work Regional (class PS) 491 (provisional) visa Sponsor declaration completed by your sponsor. proof that your sponsor is an eligible relative. proof that your sponsor has turned 18. proof that your sponsor is an Australian citizen, permanent resident or an eligible New Zealand citizen. proof that your sponsor is usually resident in a designated area of Australia. To prove that your sponsor is an Australian citizen, permanent resident or an eligible New Zealand citizen, provide: citizenship certificate, or. passport bio-data page.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Sponsor documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Sponsor documents: To prove your sponsor is usually resident in a designated area of Australia, documents you can provide include, but are not limited to: drivers licence. mortgage/tenancy agreements. utility bills. To prove the sponsor's relationship with you, documents you can provide include, but are not limited to: birth certificate. marriage certificates. death certificates. adoption certificates. family status certificates or family books if officially issued and maintained.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Nomination documents
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Nomination documents: If you are being nominated you do not need to provide evidence of this with your application.

Upload your written notification or your forms to ImmiAccount.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Translate
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Translate: Have all non-English documents translated into English. Provide original and translated documents in your application. Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters. Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited. But on each translation, they must include their: full name. address and telephone number. qualifications and experience in the language they are translating. These details must be in English. Note: You do not need to have any documents certified.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Scan or photograph
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Scan or photograph: Scan or photograph all documents (English and non-English) in colour. The scans and photos must be clear. If a document is more than 1 page, save it all as 1 file.

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Apply for the visa
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Apply for the visa: When you have your invitation you can apply online. You can be in or outside Australia. You have 60 days from the date of your invitation to apply for the visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Apply for this visa online in ImmiAccount
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Apply for this visa online in ImmiAccount: Log into your SkillSelect account. In SkillSelect, click on the 'Apply for visa' button. This will take you to our online system, ImmiAccount. Log in or create an ImmiAccount. Your ImmiAccount login and password will not be the same as your SkillSelect login and password. Attach your documents. Pay the first visa application charge. We will not process your application until you pay this first instalment of the visa application charge. Note your transaction reference number (TRN). Each family member must have their application charge paid and documents attached to their application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), After you apply: We will let you know when we have received your application. If you are granted a bridging visa you will receive notification of your visa grant.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Status updates
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Status updates: We do not give updates on applications within the standard processing time. You can check if we need more information from you in ImmiAccount.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Travel after you apply
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Travel after you apply: If you are in Australia, you don't have to tell us if you want to travel outside Australia while we process your application. This is because you can be outside Australia when we make a decision. But if you leave Australia, make sure your visa allows you to return. To see if you can return on your current visa, check VEVO. Learn about visa expiry. If you applied outside Australia, don't arrange travel to Australia, leave your job or sell your home until we advise you in writing that you have been granted the visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Health exams
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Health exams: If you didn't have health examinations before you applied, we will let you know if you need them. Check ImmiAccount.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Biometrics
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Biometrics: We might ask for biometrics (fingerprints and photo). We will let you know if you need to provide them.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Attach more information
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Attach more information: If you did not attach all documents when you applied, attach them as soon as you can to your ImmiAccount. We might also ask you to provide more information, however we are not obliged to do so and may make a decision on your application without asking for more documents.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Stay lawful
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Stay lawful: If you are in Australia, make sure you stay lawful by holding a valid visa while we process your application. When you applied for this visa, you were granted a Bridging visa A (BVA). If your current visa expires before we decide on your application, the BVA will come into effect. You can stay in Australia on the BVA while we process your new visa application. Do not ask to have the visa you currently hold cancelled. If your visa is cancelled: you will be staying in Australia unlawfully. your BVA will cease. Learn more about visa expiry.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Pay the second instalment
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Pay the second instalment: If you need to pay a second instalment, pay it when we send you the invoice.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Add family
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Add family: You can add dependent children to your application after you apply but before we decide on your visa. Use Form 1436 Adding an additional applicant after lodgement, pay using ImmiAccount, attach the form and supporting documents to your ImmiAccount. Family members who apply for the visa must meet our health and character requirements. Family members who are not coming to Australia do have to meet our character requirement and might have to meet our health requirement.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Newborn child
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Newborn child: If your child is born after you submit your application but before we decide on your visa, you must tell us as soon as possible. Find out what to do your child is born after you apply.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Subsequent entrants
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Subsequent entrants: If we grant you the visa, your family members might be able to apply to join you in Australia later as subsequent entrants.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Mistakes on your application
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Mistakes on your application: You must tell us as soon as possible if you made a mistake on your application. Complete Form 1023 Notification of incorrect answers and attach it to your application in ImmiAccount.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Help with your application: Let us know if you no longer want someone to: receive your correspondence - complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient. provide immigration advice - complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person. abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Tell us if things change: Things you need to let us know about after you have applied include: changes to your phone number, email, address or passport. changes to your marital or de facto status. the birth of a child. you want to withdraw your application. See how to tell us if your situation changes.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU
