title: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491): Visa outcome
abstract: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional) visa (subclass 491), Visa outcome: You can be in or outside Australia when we decide your visa application but not in immigration clearance. We will let you know our decision in writing. If we grant your visa, we will tell you: your visa grant number. the date your visa starts. your visa conditions, if applicable. Keep a copy of the decision. If we refuse your visa, we will tell you: why we refused the visa. whether you have a right to a review of the decision. We will not refund the application charge if we refuse your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

abstract: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820), With this visa you can: live, work and study in Australia while we process your permanent Partner visa. travel to and from Australia as many times as you want. attend free English language classes provided by the Adult Migrant English Program if you are eligible. apply for access to Australia’s public health care scheme, Medicare.

title: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820): Cost
abstract: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820), Cost: From for most applicants. From for Prospective Marriage visa (subclass 300) holders. Concessions apply in limited circumstances. Cost concession for eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste Partner visa applicants. From 1 July 2026, a lower visa cost applies to eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste citizens who lodge a valid visa application. See About this visa. We cannot provide any further updates on your application's progress. You can check the status of your visa application and if you have provided all supporting documents through ImmiAccount. To see current standard processing times for this visa refer to Global processing times. The estimated timeframe is based on how long it has taken to process recently decided applications. It does not guarantee that your application will be decided within the current standard processing timeframe.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820): Status updates
abstract: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820), Status updates: As Partner visa applications can have long visa processing times, you should update your documents and evidence of your relationship regularly through ImmiAccount. Before you get your police certificates and complete your health examinations, you should refer to the Visa processing times. We may ask you to provide them again if they expire before we decide your visa. You can find the answers to common questions about this visa at Partner Visa Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820): Travel
abstract: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820), Travel: You can travel outside Australia and return if your current visa lets you. If you hold a bridging visa see Travel on a bridging visa (homeaffairs.gov.au). If you leave Australia, make sure you have a valid visa to return.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

abstract: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820), Add family members: You can add a dependent child to your application before we decide on your visa. Your child must be in Australia. Complete Form 1436 - Adding an additional applicant after lodgement (481KB PDF) and attach it to your ImmiAccount. After you have attached the form, let us know by using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form. Newborn children. If you have a baby, you will need to let us know. For more information, see You had a baby. After you have updated us in ImmiAccount, let us know by using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form.

title: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820): Tell us if things change
abstract: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820), Tell us if things change: Tell us if things change after you apply but before we have made a decision. Things you need to let us know about include: changes to your marital or de facto status. the birth of a child. any other changes relevant to your application. a request to withdraw your application. For more information, see Change in your situation. If you are unable to upload the relevant documents to your application in ImmiAccount, you need to contact us using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form.

title: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820): If your relationship ends
abstract: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820), If your relationship ends: Depending on your situation you may need to complete the Notification of Relationship Cessation form in ImmiAccount. To confirm, check Your relationship has changed. Your online safety. To ensure your personal safety online we recommend that you: change your ImmiAccount password as soon as possible. do not use saved passwords to access your ImmiAccount. change your email password or consider setting up a new email account. To see how you can increase your personal safety you can use the eSafety Commissioner’s online safety checklist.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820): If your relationship ends
abstract: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820), If your relationship ends: If you do not have access to ImmiAccount, you can notify us using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form. You may still be eligible for a temporary and permanent visa if your relationship ends or your partner dies. All information you provide is confidential. If you are experiencing domestic and family violence, we may be able to help you. You may still be eligible for the grant of your temporary and permanent visa. For more information, see Family Violence Provisions.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820): Stay lawful
abstract: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820), Stay lawful: Make sure you stay lawful by holding a valid visa while we process your application. If you held a valid substantive visa when you applied for your partner visa, you were granted a Bridging visa A (BVA). If your current visa expires before we decide your application, the BVA will start. You can stay in Australia on the BVA while we process your new visa application. See what to do if your visa has expired or is about to expire.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820): No longer need help with your application
abstract: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820), No longer need help with your application: Let us know if you no longer want someone to: receive your correspondence - complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient (301KB PDF). provide immigration advice - complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person (308KB PDF). After you have attached the form to ImmiAccount, let us know by using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820): Mistakes on your application
abstract: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820), Mistakes on your application: Let us know as soon as you can if you have made a mistake on your application. title: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820): Visa outcome
abstract: Partner visa (temporary, subclass 820), Visa outcome: You can be in or outside Australia when we decide your temporary visa application. We will let you know our decision in writing. If we grant your visa, we will tell you: your visa grant number. the date your visa starts. your visa conditions, if applicable. Keep a copy of the decision. If we refuse your visa, we will tell you: why we refused the visa. whether you have a right to a review of the decision. We will not refund the application fee if we refuse your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): With this visa you can
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), With this visa you can: In addition to what you can do on your subclass 820 visa, you can: live, work and study in Australia indefinitely. sponsor eligible family members to come to Australia. apply for Australian citizenship, if eligible.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): How long you can stay
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), How long you can stay: Permanently.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Cost
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Cost: You paid for this visa when you made your applications for the temporary and permanent Partner visas.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): You must
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), You must: hold a temporary Partner visa (subclass 820) or Dependent Child visa (subclass 445). in most cases, continue to be in a genuine and ongoing relationship with your sponsor. Help with your visa. If you are getting help with your visa, make sure you read information on Who can help with your visa application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Visa requirements
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Visa requirements: You must hold either a Partner visa (subclass 820) or a Dependent Child (subclass 445) visa. 2 years must have passed since you applied for the subclass 820 and 801 visas for you to be eligible to be assessed for the permanent subclass 801 visa. You can check the date you submitted your applications in ImmiAccount. We might grant you the permanent subclass 801 visa in less than 2 years if you were in a long-term partner relationship with your sponsor when you applied for the subclass 820 and 801 visas.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Continue to meet relationship requirements
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Continue to meet relationship requirements: You must continue to be the spouse or de facto partner of the same person who sponsored you for the temporary Partner visa. You might still be eligible for the permanent visa if your relationship ends or your partner dies before we grant the permanent visa. For more information, see Your relationship has changed. If you are experiencing domestic and family violence, we may be able to help you. You may still be eligible for the grant of your permanent visa. For more information, see Domestic and family violence and your visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Meet our health requirement
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Meet our health requirement: You and any members of the family unit, including dependent children who apply for the visa with you, must continue to meet our health requirement. Family members who do not come with you to Australia might also need to meet our health requirement. If you had health examinations for your subclass 820 visa, we will let you know if you need to undertake them again or if more health checks are needed. For more information on health related risks to the Australian community including Polio see risks to public health.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Have no debt to the Australian government
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Have no debt to the Australian government: If you or any family members owe the Australian government money, you or they must pay it back or arrange to pay it back. This may include family members who do not come with you to Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Best interests of the child
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Best interests of the child: We might not grant this visa if it is not in the best interests of an applicant under 18.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Before you apply
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Before you apply: If we granted you a permanent Partner visa (subclass 801) immediately after we granted your temporary Partner visa (subclass 820), you do not have to do anything else. If we did not, you need to provide further documents. To check which visa you currently hold, use VEVO.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Get help with your application
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Get help with your application: You can appoint anyone to receive documents on your behalf relating to your visa application. To appoint someone to receive your correspondence, use Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient. If you need help with your application, you can appoint someone to give you immigration assistance. A person who gives you immigration assistance can: discuss your application with us. give us information. send and receive correspondence about your application. We treat any correspondence they send as if it came from you.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Get help with your application
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Get help with your application: It is important to provide your own contact details in case we need to contact you directly about your application. The partner visa application form will ask you for your own phone number and email address. If you appoint someone to give you immigration assistance they must be one of the following: A registered migration agent. A legal practitioner. An exempt person. To appoint someone to provide immigration assistance, use Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person. For more information, see who can help you with your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Gather and prepare your documents
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Gather and prepare your documents: You are eligible for consideration of the permanent Partner visa two years after you apply for the temporary and permanent Partner visas. You can check the date you submitted your application in ImmiAccount. Once two years have passed since you first applied, you can submit your documents for the permanent stage of your Partner visa. Do not send them before this time. Make sure you provide all required information with your application. Applications with all required information can be processed faster. Ensure that all information you provide is accurate.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Gather and prepare your documents
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Gather and prepare your documents: As a visa applicant, you must prove your identity and provide true information with your application. For more information see Providing accurate information.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Identity documents
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Identity documents: Provide a copy of the pages of your most recent passport showing your photo, personal details, signature, passport issue and expiry dates.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Character documents
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Character documents: To show that you meet our character requirements you may need to provide a current Australian police certificate. You usually need to provide this police certificate for the permanent stage of your Partner visa if you did not attach one with your subclass 820 application. We may ask you to provide a new Australian police certificate if your previous certificate has expired. For immigration purposes, police certificates are valid for 12 months from the issue date. We only accept complete disclosure National Police Certificates issued by the Australian Federal Police.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Character documents
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Character documents: We do not accept standard disclosure certificates or national police certificates issued by Australian state or territory police. To get an Australian police certificate see National Police Checks. You also need to provide an overseas police certificate from any country, including your home country, where you spent a total of 12 months or more since the grant of your 820 visa. To get an overseas police certificate, see Offices outside Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Evidence of your relationship
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Evidence of your relationship: You must provide evidence that you continue to be the spouse or de facto partner of the same person who sponsored you for the temporary Partner visa. In support of your visa application, you can provide: relationship documents. supporting evidence of your relationship.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Relationship documents
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Relationship documents: Attach to your ImmiAccount a Commonwealth statutory declaration form. This form must be completed by your sponsor with information about any of the following: Whether you and your spouse or de facto partner have a mutual commitment, to the exclusion of all others. Whether your relationship is genuine and continuing. Whether you live together or don't live permanently apart. When your relationship began and how long you have lived together for. The financial commitments you and your partner share.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Relationship documents
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Relationship documents: The nature of your household (including any joint responsibility for the care and support of children). The social aspects of your relationship. The nature of your commitment to each other. Your plans for the future. If you are married, provide your marriage certificate or other evidence that your marriage is valid in Australia. If you are a de facto partner, provide proof of your de facto relationship.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Supporting evidence of your relationship
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Supporting evidence of your relationship: To show you are still in a relationship with your spouse or de facto partner, you can provide the below supporting evidence of your relationship. Finances. Evidence you and your partner share financial matters. This evidence can include: joint mortgage or lease documents. joint loan documents for major assets like homes, cars or major appliances. joint bank account statements. household bills in both names. Your household. Evidence you and your partner share domestic matters.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Supporting evidence of your relationship
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Supporting evidence of your relationship: This evidence can include: a statement about how you share housework. household bills in both names. mail or emails addressed to you both. documents that show joint responsibility for children. documents that prove your living arrangements. Social matters. Evidence that others know about your relationship. You must provide statements from 2 witnesses who: are 18 years old or older. know you and your spouse or partner. know about your relationship.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Supporting evidence of your relationship
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Supporting evidence of your relationship: Statements from witnesses can be done by completing Form 888 - Supporting statement in relation to a Partner or Prospective Marriage visa application. If the witness is an Australian citizen or permanent resident, provide evidence of this such as a passport or birth certificate. Evidence can also include: joint invitations or evidence you go out together. proof you have friends in common. proof you have told government, public or commercial bodies about your relationship. proof you do joint sporting, cultural or social activities together. proof you travel together. Commitment.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Supporting evidence of your relationship
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Supporting evidence of your relationship: Evidence you are committed to a long-term relationship with each other. This evidence must show that you: have knowledge of each other’s background, family situation or other personal details. have combined your personal matters. stay in touch when apart. are not related by family. You can also provide the terms of your wills as evidence.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Family members
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Family members: For every family member who currently holds a subclass 820 or 445 visa, provide copies of: their passport. documents that show changes to their situation. police certificates, if applicable, for dependents 16 years old or older.

abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Prepare your documents: Translate. Have all documents translated into English. Provide original and translated documents in your application. Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters. Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited. But on each translation, they must include their: full name. address and telephone number. qualifications and experience in the language they are translating. These details must be in English. Scan or photograph. Scan or photograph all documents (English and non-English) in colour.

title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): Apply for the visa
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), Apply for the visa: You are eligible for consideration of the permanent Partner visa two years after you apply for the temporary and permanent Partner visas. title: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801): How to apply
abstract: Partner visa (permanent, subclass 801), How to apply: Login to ImmiAccount. Select ‘New application’. Select ‘Family’. Select ‘Stage 2 – Permanent Partner Visa Assessment’. Attach documents. Attach a document only once, even if you are using it to show more than one thing. Clearly label your documents. You can attach up to 100 documents for each person on your application. The attachment limit cannot be increased. If you reach the attachment limit for an applicant, you can attach more documents to other clients on the application. For more information see Applying online in ImmiAccount. Frequently asked questions.

If we refuse your visa, we will tell you why we refused the visa and whether you have a right to a review of the decision. We will not refund the application fee if we refuse your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): With this visa you can
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), With this visa you can: live, work and study in Australia while we process your permanent Partner visa. travel to and from Australia as many times as you want. attend free English language classes provided by the Adult Migrant English Program if you are eligible. apply for access to Australia's public health care scheme, Medicare.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): How long you can stay
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), How long you can stay: Temporarily until your permanent Partner visa (subclass 100) application is finalised or you withdraw your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Cost
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Cost: Concessions apply in limited circumstances. Cost concession for eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste Partner visa applicants. From 1 July 2026, a lower visa cost applies to eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste citizens who lodge a valid visa application. See About this visa. To work out what your visa will cost, use the Visa Pricing Estimator. The estimator does not take into account other costs relating to your visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): You must
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), You must: be in a genuine relationship with your spouse or de facto partner who is an Australian citizen, permanent resident or eligible New Zealand citizen. have your spouse or de facto partner sponsor you. be outside Australia when you apply for this visa, along with family that apply with you. be in or outside Australia when we decide your temporary visa application. Help with your visa. If you are getting help with your visa, before you pay someone, read information on Who can help with your visa application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): To be eligible for this visa you must:
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), To be eligible for this visa you must:: not had a visa cancelled or an application refused. be outside Australia when you apply. have a sponsor. be the right age. meet relationship requirements. meet our health requirement. meet our character requirement. have no debt to the Australian Government. sign the Australian values statement. best interests of the child.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Not had a visa cancelled or an application refused
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Not had a visa cancelled or an application refused: We will consider your immigration history when we make a decision on your application, which means you might not be eligible for this visa if you have had a visa cancelled or refused. In some circumstances you may still apply for a permanent visa if you have had a visa cancelled or an application refused, see Can I go to Australia. If you want immigration assistance, see Who can help with your visa application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Be outside Australia when you apply
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Be outside Australia when you apply: You must be outside Australia when you apply for this visa. Family who apply with you must also be outside Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Have a sponsor
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Have a sponsor: You and anyone who applies for the visa with you must have a sponsor when you lodge your application and when you are on this visa. Your sponsor is usually your partner. We must approve your sponsor. You cannot change your sponsor. The person who sponsors you when you apply for the visa must be the same person who sponsors you for 2 years after we grant your temporary partner visa (subclass 309). Your sponsor should apply to sponsor you as soon as possible after you apply for this visa. Select the 'For Sponsors' switch at the top of this page for information about sponsorship.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Be the right age
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Be the right age: Married applicants must usually be 18 or older when they apply. This is because usually, you must be 18 or older to be married under Australian law. Applicants in de facto relationships must be 18 or older when they apply.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Meet relationship requirements
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Meet relationship requirements: In most cases, you must be the spouse or de facto partner of an: Australian citizen. Australian permanent resident or. eligible New Zealand citizen. This applies when you make your application and when your application is being decided. If you are experiencing domestic and family violence, we may be able to help you. You can apply for consideration to be granted your temporary and permanent visa. For more information, see Family Violence Provisions. For more information, see Changes in your situation. To be a spouse, you must be in a married relationship. Forced marriage.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Meet relationship requirements
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Meet relationship requirements: Forced marriage is when a person (or both people) gets married without freely and fully consenting. They may be tricked, threatened or pressured into getting married, or they are incapable of understanding the nature and effect of a marriage ceremony, for reasons including age or mental capacity. Forced marriage is a crime in Australia. If you or someone you know is in, or at risk of, a forced marriage you can seek help. For more information, see Forced marriage | Attorney-General's Department. De facto partners. To be a de facto partner, you must be in a de facto relationship.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Meet relationship requirements
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Meet relationship requirements: Usually you must be in your de facto relationship for at least 12 months immediately before you apply for this visa. Time spent dating or in an online relationship might not count as being in a de facto relationship. The 12-month requirement will not apply if you can show us compelling and compassionate circumstances exist for you to be granted the provisional Partner visa (subclass 309).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Meet relationship requirements
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Meet relationship requirements: The 12-month requirement also will not apply if: your de facto partner holds or held a permanent humanitarian visa; and. your de facto relationship existed before we granted their visa; and. your de facto partner told us about the relationship before we granted their visa. It also will not apply if: you are in a de facto relationship with a partner who is an applicant for a permanent humanitarian visa, or. you have registered your relationship with an Australian State or Territory authority such as a registry of births, deaths and marriages.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Meet our health requirement
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Meet our health requirement: You and any family members who apply for the visa with you must meet our health requirement. We might ask for health information about family not coming to Australia with you.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Meet our character requirement
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Meet our character requirement: You and family members aged 16 years and over who apply for the visa with you must meet our character requirement. We might ask for character information about family not coming to Australia with you.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Have no debt to the Australian government
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Have no debt to the Australian government: If you or any family members owe the Australian Government money, you or they must pay it back or arrange to pay it back. This may include family members who do not accompany you to Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Sign the Australian values statement
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Sign the Australian values statement: You and any family members who apply with you who are 18 years of age or older, must: have read, or had explained to you, the Life in Australia booklet and. sign an Australian Values Statement that confirms you will respect the Australian way of life and obey Australian laws.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Best interests of the child
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Best interests of the child: We might not grant this visa if it is not in the best interests of an applicant under 18.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Before you apply
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Before you apply: There are things you need to know and might need to do before you apply.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Processing times
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Processing times: Processing times for Partner visa applications vary. Partner visa applicants may experience longer processing times than expected. For an indication of processing times for this visa, use the visa processing time guide tool. This will show the processing times for recently decided applications. It is a guide only and not specific to your application. Applications are processed according to Ministerial Direction 117. For more information, see Family visa processing priorities.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Processing times
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Processing times: You can find the answers to common questions about Partner visa processing times at Partner Visa Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Get help with your application
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Get help with your application: You can appoint anyone to receive correspondence relating to your visa application. To appoint someone to receive your correspondence, use Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient (301KB PDF). If you need help with your application, you can appoint someone to give you immigration assistance. A person who gives you immigration assistance can: discuss your application with us. give us information. send and receive correspondence about your application. We treat any correspondence they send as if it came from you.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Get help with your application
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Get help with your application: If you appoint someone to give you immigration assistance they must be: a registered migration agent. a legal practitioner. an exempt person. To appoint someone to provide immigration assistance, use Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person (225KB PDF). For more information, see who can help you with your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Gather and prepare your documents
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Gather and prepare your documents: You should provide all required information with your application, or as soon as possible after you apply. You have the option to get your police certificates before you apply. However, for immigration purposes, police certificates are valid for 12 months from the date of issue. Before you get your police certificates, you should refer to the Visa processing times. We may ask you to provide them again if they expire before we decide your visa. Ensure that all information you provide is accurate.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Gather and prepare your documents
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Gather and prepare your documents: As a visa applicant, you must prove your identity and provide true information with your application. For more information see Providing accurate information. Your sponsor should apply to sponsor you as soon as possible after you apply for this visa. Select the ‘For Sponsors’ switch at the top of this page for information about sponsorship.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Identity documents
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Identity documents: Provide a birth certificate showing the names of both parents. If you cannot provide this, provide the identification page for one of the following: family book showing the names of both parents. identification document issued by the government. court-issued document that proves your identity. family census register.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Identity documents
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Identity documents: Also provide: the pages of your current passport showing your photo, personal details and passport issue and expiry dates. a national identity card, if you have one. proof of change of name, if applicable, such as: a marriage or divorce certificate. change of name documents from an Australian Registry of Births, Deaths and Marriages, or the relevant overseas authority. documents that show other names you have been known by.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Evidence of relationships
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Evidence of relationships: You need to provide evidence of: your relationship with your partner. any former relationships. any dependants you have.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Your relationship with your partner
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Your relationship with your partner: You must provide evidence of your relationship with your spouse or de facto partner. Relationship history. Tell us in writing about: how, when and where you first met. how the relationship developed. when you moved in together, got engaged or married. what you do together. time you spent apart. significant events in the relationship. your plans for the future. Relationship documents. If you are married, provide your marriage certificate or other evidence that your marriage is valid in Australia. If you are a de facto partner, you need to provide evidence of your de facto relationship.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Your relationship with your partner
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Your relationship with your partner: Evidence of your de facto relationship. In addition to documents proving your relationship, show us you have been in your de facto relationship for at least 12 months before you applied for this visa. If you haven't been with your de facto partner for 12 months, you can: provide evidence you have registered your relationship with an Australian State/Territory births, deaths and marriages agency or. tell us in writing about any compelling and compassionate circumstances for us to grant the visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Supporting evidence of the relationship
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Supporting evidence of the relationship: Finances. Evidence you and your partner share financial matters. Evidence can include: joint mortgage or lease documents. joint loan documents for major assets like homes, cars or major appliances. joint bank account statements. household bills in both names. Your household. Evidence you and your partner share domestic matters. Evidence can include: a statement about how you share housework. household bills in both names. mail or emails addressed to you both. documents that show joint responsibility for children. documents that prove your living arrangements. Social matters.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Supporting evidence of the relationship
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Supporting evidence of the relationship: Evidence that others know about your relationship. You must provide statements from 2 witnesses who: are 18 years old or older. know you and your spouse or de facto partner. know about your relationship. Statements from witnesses can be done by completing Form 888 – Supporting statement in relation to a Partner or Prospective Marriage visa application (241KB PDF). If the witness is an Australian citizen or permanent resident, provide evidence of this such as a passport or birth certificate.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Supporting evidence of the relationship
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Supporting evidence of the relationship: Evidence can also include: joint invitations or evidence you go out together. proof you have friends in common. proof you have told government, public or commercial bodies about your relationship. proof you do joint sporting, cultural or social activities together. proof you travel together. Commitment. Evidence you are committed to a long-term relationship with each other. Evidence must show that you: have knowledge of each other’s background, family situation or other personal details. have combined your personal matters. stay in touch when apart. are not related by family.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Supporting evidence of the relationship
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Supporting evidence of the relationship: You can also provide the terms of your wills as evidence.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Former relationships
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Former relationships: If you have previously been married, widowed, divorced or permanently separated, provide divorce documents, death certificates, separation documents or statutory declarations.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Dependants under 18
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Dependants under 18: For each of the members of the family unit under 18 years old applying with you, provide: identity documents. evidence of your relationship with your dependant, like a birth or marriage certificate. health examinations. character documents, if the dependant is 16 or 17 years of age. adoption papers or parental court orders, if applicable. evidence of enrolment at school, college or university, if applicable. evidence of sole custody, if applicable. Parental responsibility documents.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Dependants under 18
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Dependants under 18: You must get consent for any applicant under 18 years of age to migrate to Australia from anyone who: has a legal right to decide where the child lives and. is not coming to Australia with the child. They must complete Form 1229 Consent form to grant an Australian visa to a child under the age of 18 years (240KB PDF). Include: an identity document that shows the signature and photo of the person who completed the form, such as a passport or driver’s licence. adoption papers or other court documents, if applicable.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Dependants under 18
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Dependants under 18: Alternatively, you can show us: an Australian court order that allows your child to migrate to Australia, or. that the laws of the child's home country allow them to leave their home country permanently.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Dependants over 18
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Dependants over 18: To include members of the family unit who are over 18 in your visa application, they must be: over 18 years of age but not yet turned 23, and dependent on you or your partner, or. over 23 years of age and unable to earn a living to support themselves due to physical or cognitive limitations and dependent on you or your partner. Provide: identity documents. documents about their other relationships, if applicable. health examinations. character documents. You must also provide evidence the child is dependent on you.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Dependants over 18
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Dependants over 18: This includes: evidence of your relationship with the dependent such as a birth certificate or adoption papers. evidence of financial dependence such as bank statements, money transfers and rent receipts. a completed Form 47a Details of a child or other dependent family member aged 18 years or over (241KB PDF). If the child is aged 23 or is likely to turn 23 while your application is being processed, you must also provide a report from a qualified medical practitioner that states they are dependent on you or your partner due to the total or partial loss of their bodily or mental functions.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Prepare your documents
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Prepare your documents: Translate. Have all documents translated into English. Provide original and translated documents in your application. Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters. Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited. On each translation, they must include their: full name. address and telephone number. qualifications and experience in the language they are translating. These details must be in English. Scan or photograph. Scan or photograph all documents (English and non-English) in colour.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Prepare your documents
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Prepare your documents: The scans and photos must be clear enough to read. If a document is more than one page, save it all as one file. You do not need to have any documents certified.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Apply for the visa
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Apply for the visa: You must apply: online. outside Australia. Using our website and protections to your privacy. We take our obligation to protect your privacy seriously. We provide a secure online environment, but you can do more to ensure your personal safety online: Make sure you give us your contact details when you apply for your visa and tell us if they have changed.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Apply for the visa
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Apply for the visa: We may need to contact you directly even if you have: nominated your sponsor’s email address for all electronic correspondence. appointed your sponsor or someone else to receive your correspondence as your authorised recipient. appointed someone to give you immigration assistance. Protect your ImmiAccount, email account and passwords. Don’t share them with anyone. For more information see Using our website.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): How to apply
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), How to apply: Login or create an ImmiAccount. Select ‘New application’. Select ‘Family’. Select ‘Stage 1 – Partner or Prospective Marriage Visa’. Attach documents. Pay the application charge. We will not process your application until you pay. Note the Transaction Reference Number (TRN). Your sponsor will need the TRN to apply for sponsorship. Select the ‘For Sponsors’ switch at the top of this page for information on how to apply as a sponsor. Attach a document only once, even if you are using it to show more than one thing. Clearly label your documents.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): How to apply
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), How to apply: You can attach up to 100 documents for each person on your application. The attachment limit cannot be increased. If you reach the attachment limit for an applicant, you can attach more documents to other clients on the application. For more information see Applying online in ImmiAccount. Frequently asked questions. A list of common questions and answers is available at Partner Visa Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): After you apply
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), After you apply: We will let you know when we have received your application. As Partner applications can have long visa processing times, you should update your documents and evidence of your relationship regularly through ImmiAccount. Before you get your police certificates and complete your health examinations, you should refer to Visa processing times. We may ask you to provide them again if they expire before we decide your visa. The results of your health assessment are valid for 12 months from the time you complete your examinations. If we ask you to sign a health undertaking, this is for 6 months.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): After you apply
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), After you apply: For immigration purposes, police certificates are valid for 12 months from the date of issue.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Be sponsored
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Be sponsored: You and anyone who applies for the visa with you must have a sponsor when you lodge your application and when you are on this visa. After you apply for this visa, give your sponsor your Transaction Reference Number (TRN) or application ID. Your sponsor can then apply to sponsor you. Select the ‘For Sponsors’ switch at the top of this page for information about sponsorship.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Health examinations
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Health examinations: You need to have health examinations. The results of your health assessment are valid for 12 months from the date you complete your examinations. If we ask you to sign a health undertaking, this is valid for 6 months. Before you complete your health examinations, you should refer to the Visa processing times. We may ask you to provide them again if they expire before we decide your visa. To organise your health examinations, see What health examinations you need. For more information on health requirements see Health.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Character documents
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Character documents: If you have spent a total of 12 months or more in Australia in the last 10 years (since you turned 16), you must provide an Australian police certificate. We only accept complete disclosure National Police Certificates issued by the Australian Federal Police. We do not accept standard disclosure certificates or national police certificates issued by Australian state or territory police. To get an Australian police certificate see National Police Checks.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Character documents
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Character documents: Also provide: a police certificate from every country where you spent a total of 12 months or more in, in the last 10 years since you turned 16. military service records or discharge papers if you served in the armed forces of any country. To get an overseas police certificate, see Services outside Australia. For immigration purposes, police certificates are valid for 12 months from the issue date. Before deciding when to obtain your police certificates, you should refer to the Visa processing times. We may ask you to provide them again if they expire before we decide your visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Character documents
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Character documents: Complete and attach to your application Form 80 Personal particulars for assessment including character assessment (596KB PDF). Further information is available at: Character requirements for visas.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Status updates
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Status updates: Do not contact us if your application is within the current standard processing time. We cannot provide any further updates on your application's progress. You can check the status of your visa application and if you have provided all supporting documents through ImmiAccount. To see current standard processing times for this visa refer to Global processing times. The estimated timeframe is based on how long it has taken to process recently decided applications. It does not guarantee that your application will be decided within the current standard processing timeframe.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Status updates
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Status updates: As Partner visa applications can have long visa processing times, you should update your documents and evidence of your relationship regularly through ImmiAccount. Before you get your police certificates and complete your health examinations, you should refer to the Visa processing times. We may ask you to provide them again if they expire before we decide your visa. You can find the answers to common questions about this visa at Partner Visa Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Travel
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Travel: Do not arrange to travel to Australia on this visa until we let you know, in writing, that we have granted you the subclass 309 visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU
