abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Attach more information: For more information on attaching documents in ImmiAccount see Applying online in ImmiAccount. If you are unable to upload the relevant documents to your application in ImmiAccount, you need to contact us using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Add family members
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Add family members: You can add a dependent child to your application before we decide your visa. Your child must be outside Australia. Complete and attach to your ImmiAccount Form 1436 - Adding an additional applicant after lodgement (481KB PDF). After you have attached the form, let us know by using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form. We can grant your child the subclass 309 visa if they are members of the family unit and meet all other criteria for grant. Newborn Children. If you have a baby, you will need to let us know. For more information, see You had a baby.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Tell us if your details have changed
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Tell us if your details have changed: See here for changes to your contact details, address or passport.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Tell us if things change
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Tell us if things change: Tell us if things change after you apply but before we have made a decision. Things you need to let us know about include: changes to your marital or de facto status. the birth of a child. any other changes relevant to your application. a request to withdraw your application. For more information, see Change in your situation. If you are unable to upload the relevant documents to your application in ImmiAccount, you need to contact us using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): If your relationship ends
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), If your relationship ends: Depending on your situation you may need to complete the Notification of Relationship Cessation form in ImmiAccount. To confirm, check Your relationship has changed. Your online safety. To ensure your personal safety online we recommend that you: change your ImmiAccount password as soon as possible. do not use saved passwords to access your ImmiAccount. change your email password or consider setting up a new email account. To see how you can increase your personal safety you can use the eSafety Commissioner’s online safety checklist.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): If your relationship ends
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), If your relationship ends: If you do not have access to ImmiAccount, you can notify us using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form. You may still be eligible for a temporary and permanent visa if your relationship ends or your partner dies. All information you provide is confidential. If you are experiencing domestic and family violence, we may be able to help you. You may still be eligible for the grant of your temporary and permanent visa if you have entered Australia since lodging your application. For more information, see Family Violence Provisions.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Stay lawful
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Stay lawful: If you travel to Australia on a different visa while this visa application is in progress, you are responsible for ensuring that you continue to hold a valid visa for the duration of your stay.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): No longer need help with your application
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), No longer need help with your application: Let us know if you no longer want someone to: receive your correspondence - complete Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient. provide immigration advice - complete Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person. After you have attached the form to ImmiAccount, let us know by using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form. For more information see Who can help you with your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Mistakes on your application
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Mistakes on your application: Let us know as soon as you can if you have made a mistake on your application. For more information see After you apply. If you are unable to update your application in ImmiAccount, you need to contact us using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Visa outcome
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Visa outcome: New step description.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Visa outcome
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Visa outcome: You can be in or outside Australia when we decide on your temporary visa application. If your relationship ends or your partner dies, you may still be eligible for a temporary and permanent visa. For more information, see Your relationship has changed. We will tell you our decision in writing. Keep a copy of the decision. If we grant your visa, we will tell you: your visa grant number. the date your visa starts. your visa conditions, if applicable. If we refuse your visa, we will tell you: why we refused the visa. whether you have a right to a review of the decision.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309): Visa outcome
abstract: Partner visa (provisional, subclass 309), Visa outcome: We will not refund the application fee if we refuse your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): With this visa you can
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), With this visa you can: In addition to what you can do on your subclass 309 visa, you can: live, work and study in Australia indefinitely. sponsor eligible family members to come to Australia. apply for Australian citizenship if eligible.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): How long you can stay
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), How long you can stay: Permanently.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Cost
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Cost: You paid for this visa when you made your applications for the temporary and permanent Partner visas.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): You must
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), You must: hold a temporary Partner (Provisional) visa (subclass 309) or Dependent Child visa (subclass 445 ). in most cases, continue to be in a genuine and ongoing relationship with your sponsor. Help with your visa. If you are getting help with your visa, make sure you read information on Who can help with your visa application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Visa requirements
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Visa requirements: You must hold either a Partner (Provisional) (subclass 309) or a Dependent Child (subclass 445) visa. 2 years must have passed since you applied for the subclass 309 and 100 visas for you to be eligible to be assessed for the permanent subclass 100 visa. You can check the date you submitted your application in ImmiAccount.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Visa requirements
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Visa requirements: We might grant you the permanent subclass 100 visa in less than 2 years if either: you were in a long-term partner relationship with your sponsor when you applied for the subclass 309 and 100 visas. your sponsor is, or was, the holder of a permanent humanitarian visa and before that permanent visa was granted, was in a married relationship or de facto relationship with you. You must have informed us about your relationship before that permanent visa was granted.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Continue to meet relationship requirements
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Continue to meet relationship requirements: You must continue to be the spouse or de facto partner of the same person who sponsored you for the temporary Partner visa. You might still be eligible for the permanent visa if your relationship ends or your partner dies before we grant the permanent visa. For more information, see Your relationship has changed. If you are experiencing domestic and family violence, we may be able to help you. You may still be eligible for the grant of your permanent visa. For more information, see Domestic and family violence and your visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Meet our health requirement
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Meet our health requirement: You and any members of the family unit, including dependent children who apply for the visa with you, must continue to meet our health requirement. Family members who do not come with you to Australia might also need to meet our health requirement. If you had health examinations for your subclass 309 visa, we will let you know if you need to undertake them again or if more health checks are needed. For more information on health related risks to the Australian community including Polio see risks to public health.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Have no debts to the Australian Government
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Have no debts to the Australian Government: If you or any family members owe the Australian Government money, you or they must pay it back or arrange to pay it back. This may include family members who do not come with you to Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Best interests of the child
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Best interests of the child: We might not grant this visa if it is not in the best interests of an applicant under 18.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Before you apply
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Before you apply: If we granted you a permanent Partner visa (subclass 100) immediately after we granted your temporary Partner visa (subclass 309), you do not have to provide these documents or do anything else. If we did not, you need to provide further documents. To check which visa you currently hold, use VEVO.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Get help with your application
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Get help with your application: You can appoint anyone to receive documents on your behalf, relating to your visa application. To appoint someone to receive your correspondence, use Form 956A Appointment or withdrawal of an authorised recipient. If you need help with your application, you can appoint someone to give you immigration assistance. A person who gives you immigration assistance can: discuss your application with us. give us information. send and receive correspondence about your application. We treat any correspondence they send as if it came from you.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Get help with your application
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Get help with your application: It is important to provide your own contact details in case we need to contact you directly about your application. The partner visa application form will ask you for your own phone number and email address. If you appoint someone to give you immigration assistance they must be one of the following: a registered migration agent. a legal practitioner. an exempt person. To appoint someone to provide immigration assistance, use Form 956 Appointment of a registered migration agent, legal practitioner or exempt person. For more information, see who can help you with your application.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Gather and prepare your documents
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Gather and prepare your documents: You are eligible for consideration of the permanent Partner visa two years after you apply for the temporary and permanent Partner visas. You can check the date you submitted your application in ImmiAccount. Once two years have passed since you first applied, you can submit your documents for the permanent stage of your Partner visa. Do not send them before this time. Make sure you provide all required information with your application. Applications with all required information can be processed faster. Ensure that all information you provide is accurate.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Gather and prepare your documents
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Gather and prepare your documents: As a visa applicant, you must prove your identity and provide true information with your application. For more information, see Providing accurate information.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Identity documents
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Identity documents: Provide a copy of the pages of your most recent passport. It must show your photo, personal details, signature, passport issue and expiry dates.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Character documents
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Character documents: To show that you meet our character requirements you may need to provide a current Australian police certificate. You usually need to provide this police certificate for the permanent stage of your Partner visa if you did not attach one with your subclass 309 application. We may ask you to provide a new Australian police certificate, if your previous certificate has expired. For immigration purposes, police certificates are valid for 12 months from the issue date. We only accept complete disclosure National Police Certificates issued by the Australian Federal Police.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Character documents
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Character documents: We do not accept standard disclosure certificates or national police certificates issued by Australian state or territory police. To get an Australian police certificate see National Police Checks. You also need to provide an overseas police certificate from any country, including your home country, where you spent a total of 12 months or more since the grant of your 309 visa. To get an overseas police certificate, see Offices outside Australia.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Evidence of your relationship
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Evidence of your relationship: You must provide evidence that you continue to be the spouse or de facto partner of the same person who sponsored you for the temporary Partner visa. In support of your visa application, you can provide: relationship documents. supporting evidence of your relationship.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Relationship documents
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Relationship documents: Attach to your ImmiAccount a Commonwealth statutory declaration form. This form must be completed by your sponsor with information about any of the following: Whether you and your spouse or de facto partner have a mutual commitment, to the exclusion of all others. Whether your relationship is genuine and continuing. Whether you live together, or don't live permanently apart. When your relationship began and how long you have lived together. The financial commitments you and your partner share.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Relationship documents
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Relationship documents: The nature of your household (including any joint responsibility for the care and support of children). The social aspects of your relationship. The nature of your commitment to each other. Your plans for the future. If you are married, provide your marriage certificate or other evidence that your marriage is valid in Australia. If you are a de facto partner, provide proof of your de facto relationship.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Supporting evidence of your relationship
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Supporting evidence of your relationship: To show you are still in a relationship with your partner, you can provide the below supporting evidence of your relationship. Finances. Evidence you and your partner share financial matters. This evidence can include: joint mortgage or lease documents. joint loan documents for major assets like homes, cars or major appliances. joint bank account statements. household bills in both names. Your household. Evidence you and your partner share domestic matters.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Supporting evidence of your relationship
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Supporting evidence of your relationship: This evidence can include: a statement about how you share housework. household bills in both names. mail or emails addressed to you both. documents that show joint responsibility for children. documents that prove your living arrangements. Social matters. Evidence that others know about your relationship. You must provide statements from 2 witnesses who: are 18 years old or older. know you and your spouse or de facto partner. know about your relationship.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Supporting evidence of your relationship
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Supporting evidence of your relationship: Statements from witnesses can be done by completing Form 888 – Supporting statement in relation to a Partner or Prospective Marriage visa application. If the witness is an Australian citizen or permanent resident, provide evidence of this such as a passport or birth certificate. Evidence can also include: joint invitations or evidence you go out together. proof you have friends in common. proof you have told government, public or commercial bodies about your relationship. proof you do joint sporting, cultural or social activities together. proof you travel together. Commitment.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Supporting evidence of your relationship
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Supporting evidence of your relationship: Evidence you are committed to a long-term relationship with each other. This evidence must show that you: have knowledge of each other’s background, family situation or other personal details. have combined your personal matters. stay in touch when apart. are not related by family. You can also provide the terms of your wills as evidence.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Family members
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Family members: For every family member who currently holds a subclass 309 or 445 visa, provide copies of: their passport. documents that show changes to their situation. police certificates, if applicable, for dependents 16 years old or older.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Prepare your documents
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Prepare your documents: Translate. Have all documents translated into English. Provide original and translated documents in your application. Translators in Australia must be accredited by the National Accreditation Authority for Translators and Interpreters. Translators outside Australia do not have to be accredited. But on each translation, they must include their: full name. address and telephone number. qualifications and experience in the language they are translating. These details must be in English. Scan or photograph. Scan or photograph all documents (English and non-English) in colour.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Prepare your documents
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Prepare your documents: The scans and photos must be clear enough to read. If a document is more than one page, save it all as one file. You do not need to have any documents certified.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Apply for the visa
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Apply for the visa: You are eligible for consideration of the permanent Partner visa two years after you apply for the temporary and permanent Partner visas. Submit your documents for the permanent stage of your Partner visa once two years have passed since you first applied. Do not attach them before this time. Using our website and protections to your privacy. We take our obligation to protect your privacy seriously.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Apply for the visa
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Apply for the visa: We provide a secure online environment, but you can do more to ensure your personal safety online: Make sure you give us your contact details when you apply for your visa and tell us if they have changed. We may need to contact you directly even if you have: nominated your sponsor’s email address for all electronic correspondence. appointed your sponsor or someone else to receive your correspondence as your authorised recipient. appointed someone to give you immigration assistance. Protect your ImmiAccount, email account and passwords. Don’t share them with anyone.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Apply for the visa
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Apply for the visa: For more information see Using our website.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): How to apply
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), How to apply: Login to ImmiAccount. Select ‘New application’. Select ‘Family’. Select ‘Stage 2 – Permanent Pattner Visa Assessment’. Attach documents. Attach a document only once, even if you are using it to show more than one thing. Clearly label your documents. You can attach up to 100 documents for each person on your application. The attachment limit cannot be increased. If you reach the attachment limit for an applicant, you can attach more documents to other clients on the application. For more information see Applying online in ImmiAccount. Frequently asked questions.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): How to apply
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), How to apply: A list of common questions and answers is available at Partner Visa Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): After you apply
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), After you apply: You can track and manage your application using ImmiAccount. For help managing your application in ImmiAccount, see Applying online in ImmiAccount.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Status updates
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Status updates: Do not contact us if your application is within the current standard processing time. We cannot provide any further updates on your application's progress. You can check the status of your visa application and if you have provided all supporting documents through ImmiAccount. To see current standard processing times for this visa, see Global processing times. This estimated timeframe is based on how long it has taken to process recently decided applications. It does not guarantee that your application will be decided within the current standard processing timeframe.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Status updates
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Status updates: As Partner applications can have long visa processing times, you should update your documents and evidence of your relationship regularly through ImmiAccount. You can find the answers to common questions about this visa at Partner Visa Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Attach more information
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Attach more information: If you did not attach all required documents when you applied, attach them as soon as you can in ImmiAccount. We might ask you to provide more information. As Partner visa applications can have long visa processing times, you should update your documents and evidence of your relationship regularly through ImmiAccount. For more information on attaching documents in ImmiAccount, see Applying online in ImmiAccount. If you are unable to upload the relevant documents to your application in ImmiAccount, you need to contact us using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

title: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100): Add family members
abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Add family members: You can add a dependent child to your application before we make a decision on your permanent visa application. Your child can be in or outside Australia and must: hold a Dependent Child visa (subclass 445). be members of the family unit. meet our health requirement. meet our character requirement if they are 16 years old or older. Once your child holds a subclass 445 visa, complete and attach to your ImmiAccount, Form 1002 - Application by a subclass 445 dependent child for a permanent partner visa.
attribution: Australian Government Department of Home Affairs, CC BY 3.0 AU

abstract: Partner visa (migrant, subclass 100), Add family members: After you have attached the form to ImmiAccount, let us know by using the Partner Processing Enquiry Form. Newborn children.
